memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And the Lord God commanded the man, "You are free to eat from any tree in the garden; but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for when you eat from it you will certainly die." — Gen 2:16–17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look carefully at the order of God's words, because it tells us so much about His heart. He begins not with a prohibition but with lavish freedom: "You are free to eat from any tree in the garden." God's first word to man is generosity. A whole garden of good things is offered, and only one tree is held back. The picture is not of a stingy God guarding everything, but of a giving God who provides abundantly and asks for trust in one small thing.

That single command was a matter of love, not control. A boundary is not the opposite of care—often it is the proof of it. Just as a loving parent warns a child away from fire, God's limit was for the man's protection. To reach for the forbidden tree was to say, "I will decide for myself what is good and evil, rather than trust my Maker." And God was honest about the cost: it would bring death.

We live in a world that whispers that any limit steals our freedom. But real freedom is found inside God's good boundaries, not outside them. His commands are always for our flourishing (1 John 5:3).

Sadly, we know Adam did not obey, and death came to us all. But where the first Adam failed, Jesus—the second Adam—perfectly obeyed His Father, even to death on a cross, and won for us the life Adam lost (Rom 5:19).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you tend to see God's commands as restrictive, or as loving and protective?
- Where might God be asking you to trust Him rather than decide good and evil for yourself?
- How does Jesus' perfect obedience give you hope where Adam failed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord God, thank You that Your commands flow from love and lead to life. Help me to trust You within Your good boundaries, and thank You that Jesus obeyed perfectly where we failed. Amen.
